The 'clean' wedding concept assumes human behavior can be controlled via an invitation list. It cannot.
If he views your family as 'liabilities' rather than 'relatives,' he is telling you his long-term plan for your life.
Evaluate the future: Chronic illness and aging are inevitable. Will he 'exclude' those realities too?
A wedding is a contract ceremony. Be careful what terms you are agreeing to.
pure good vibes only? is he marrying u or starting a yoga retreat? lol.
that's cold af. your sister is probably gonna be so hurt.
lowkey, weddings ARE drama. u can't avoid it. even 'normal' people get drunk and fight.
if he's this controlling now, wait until u guys have kids. red flag city.
no cap, i'd tell him 'no sister, no wedding.' see what he does.
If you want a 'clean' wedding, just marry a robot. Very predictable, great photos.
Can I come? I don't have a diagnosis, but I am very annoying. Would I make the cut?
He’s basically asking for a wedding full of mannequins. Sounds boring.
Maybe he can hire 'security' for the vibes? Vibe-bouncers?
Seriously though, he sounds like he's trying to win an Instagram contest, not a marriage.
As someone with a chronic condition, this breaks my heart. We aren't 'bad vibes.'
Bipolar and addiction are medical issues, not personality flaws for a guest list.
He’s showing you his lack of empathy. That’s a very dangerous trait in a partner.
Does he think health is a choice? This is very concerning behavior.
Please stand up for your family. They need your support more than he needs 'perfection.'
Integrity is standing by your family when it's inconvenient. This is your first real test.
A man who wants to hide your 'messy' reality is a man who will eventually want to hide you.
Marriage is 'in sickness and in health.' He's failing that before the ceremony even starts.
Do not trade your sister's dignity for a pretty party. It’s a bad trade.
The 'vibe' of a wedding should be love, not exclusion.
I can feel the tension in your post. You're being pulled between two loves.
Your sister deserves to see you get married. Her illness doesn't change that.
Maybe he had a bad experience with a 'scene' in the past? Ask him where this fear is coming from.
Try to help him understand that 'perfection' is a lonely goal.
You are a kind person. Don't let the wedding industry turn you into someone else.
A wedding is a high-cost event. He is trying to mitigate risk. I understand the logic, but the execution is flawed.
A 'clean' list is easier to manage, but the long-term social debt you'll owe your family is massive.
If you exclude them, you are effectively declaring war on your own support network. High cost, low gain.
Is there a middle ground? A 'minder' for the sister? (Kidding, mostly).
The fiancé is treating this like a corporate product launch. It’s a category error.
My sister wasn't invited to my brother's wedding for 'drama' reasons. She hasn't spoken to him in 10 years.
The 'vibes' of that wedding were great for one day, but the family is broken forever now.
Is one day of 'no scenes' worth a lifetime of resentment?
He's being cruel. Plain and simple.
If you marry him, you're saying his vanity is more important than your family's humanity.

title: I’m 'therapy-baiting' my boyfriend to get him to do what I want.
content: I’ve learned a lot of therapy language lately—'boundaries,' 'emotional labor,' 'gaslighting.' Now, whenever we argue, I use those terms to make him feel like his reactions are 'unhealthy' or 'abusive' even when he’s just frustrated. I realized today that I’m weaponizing mental health terms just to win fights. I feel powerful, but I also feel like a monster.

replies.content: at least you're self-aware enough to know you're a manipulator. most people just call it 'healing.'
therapy speak is just the new way for smart people to be jerks. you're just following the trend.
if you keep doing it, he'll eventually catch on and then you've lost the only person who puts up with you.
win the fight, lose the guy. hope the 'power' is worth being alone.
honestly, stop going to therapy if you're just using it as a weapon manual.
Semantic weaponization is a sophisticated form of control. You are redefining reality to suit your narrative.
When you use clinical terms incorrectly, you are committing intellectual fraud for emotional gain.
A 'boundary' is a rule for YOUR behavior, not a leash for HIS. You are confusing the two.
The 'power' you feel is the result of breaking the psychological safety of the relationship. It is unsustainable.
Cease the practice immediately or you will create a 'false positive' of abuse that you cannot undo.

Oh honey, it's so easy to slip into those patterns when we're trying to protect ourselves.
Maybe you're using those words because you don't feel heard when you use 'normal' language?
It doesn't make you a 'monster,' but it is a very sad way to communicate with someone you love.
Why don't you try saying 'I feel' instead of 'You are'? It might feel less like a battle.
I'm glad you realized this. That realization is the first step toward a healthier 'you.'
therapy speak is the final boss of toxic relationships lol. u wildin.
no cap, i've had this done to me. it makes u feel like u r going crazy. stop it.
if u want him to do something, just ask? or offer a trade? way easier than a psyche op.
u r gonna end up on a 'toxic ex' tiktok thread if u keep this up.
just be real. the 'monster' feeling is your brain telling u to chill.
Can you teach me? I want to 'boundary' my boss into giving me a 4-day work week.
Weaponized therapy is like bringing a nuke to a pillow fight. A bit overkill.
If he starts going to therapy too, you guys are going to have the most articulate breakup in history.
Just call him a 'poop-head' next time. It’s more honest and less traumatic.
The power you feel is just the adrenaline of being a bit of a villain. It’s a rush, I get it.
This is actually a form of emotional abuse. You are pathologizing his normal emotions.
I’ve been on the receiving end of this. It took me years of actual therapy to recover.
You are 'gaslighting' him by telling him he's gaslighting you. It's inception-level toxic.
If you really cared about mental health, you wouldn't use it as a cheat code for arguments.
You need to be alone until you can learn to relate to people without manipulating them.
As a mental health professional, this is my literal nightmare. Please stop.
You are devaluing the very tools that are meant to help people heal.
Next time you want to use a 'therapy word,' ask yourself: 'Is this true, or is this just convenient?'
You’re creating a dynamic where he can never win, which means the relationship will never grow.
Take a break from the 'therapy' content and try some radical honesty instead.
I hear the shame in your post. It’s a heavy thing to realize you've been unkind.

Think of this as an 'unfair trade practice' in the economy of your relationship.
You are devaluing your own emotional currency. Eventually, nothing you say will have weight.
Logic says: Switch to an 'open-book' communication style. It has better long-term stability.

title: I’m addicted to my own sadness because it’s the only time people check on me.
content: I realized today that I lean into my depressive episodes because of the 'attention' I get. When I’m doing well, I’m invisible. When I’m spiraling, my phone lights up with 'Are you okay?' and 'I'm here for you' texts. I’ve started exaggerating how bad I feel just to keep the check-ins coming. I’m terrified that if I actually get better, I’ll be completely alone.

replies.content: congratulations, you've turned your mental health into a subscription service. eventually, people are gonna cancel.
if you need to be miserable to have friends, you don't have friends. you have fans of your tragedy.
the 'pity party' only works for so long before people get 'compassion fatigue.' good luck with that.
you're not just 'leaning into it,' you're actively manipulating people who care. that's low.
stop acting like a victim of your own choices. if you want attention, be interesting, not pathetic.
Oh honey, you are worthy of love even when you are happy! You don't have to suffer to be seen.
It sounds like you're very lonely. Maybe try reaching out when you're feeling good, too?
I promise people want to see you smile. They're only checking in because they're worried.
Have you spoken to a therapist about this? It's a very heavy cycle to be in.
Sending you so much love. You are enough exactly as you are, without the pain.
You are reinforcing a negative feedback loop. You are training your social circle to reward dysfunction.
This is a survival strategy based on perceived scarcity of connection. It is logically self-defeating.
You are optimizing for 'quantity' of check-ins over 'quality' of relationship. Recalibrate.
Data shows that false signaling eventually leads to total social isolation when the truth emerges.
Identify the core need. Is it 'attention' or 'validation of existence'? There is a difference.
Integrity is being honest about your joy as well as your pain. You are manipulating empathy.
Real connection is built on truth. You are building a house of cards with these exaggerations.
Ask yourself: Who am I when no one is watching? That's the person you need to heal.
You are stealing care from people who might actually be in a crisis. Think on that.
Reclaim your power. You don't need a tragedy to have a voice.
I feel this so much. I feel like 'Happy Me' is boring and 'Sad Me' is deep and interesting. It's a trap.
I worry that if I stop being 'the depressed friend,' I won't have a role in the group anymore.
It's a weird kind of high when the 'Are you okay?' texts start rolling in, isn't it?
I'm trying to post more about my wins, but they get zero likes compared to the sad posts.
You're not alone in this feeling, but we both know it's not a way to live.
Just start a podcast. It's the modern way to get attention without having to be sad.
Maybe try being 'The Funny Friend' instead? It's much less exhausting than 'The Sad Friend.'
If you exaggerating, does that mean your 'depression' is just high-level theater?
I wish people checked on me when I was sad. Mostly they just ask me to borrow my lawnmower.
Attention is a hell of a drug. Hope you find a cheaper dealer.
bruh, that's kinda dark. u r catfishing people with your own feelings lol.
i get it though, some people only care when u r down. it's a fake world out here.
maybe get a dog? they check on u 24/7 and u don't even have to cry.
if i found out my homie was faking a spiral for clout, i'd be heated.
just be real. the ones who stay for the 'boring' u are the ones that matter.
This is a symptom of 'secondary gain' in psychology. You're getting a reward for being unwell.
The 'addiction' is to the validation, not the sadness. Don't confuse the two.
I used to do this. Eventually, I realized I was just lonely, not actually as sick as I claimed.
The fear of being 'invisible' is real, but faking a fire isn't the way to get warm.
Start being there for others. The best way to be seen is to actually see people.
You are exhausting the empathy of your friends. One day, you'll really need them, and they'll be gone.
This is borderline Munchausen's but for social media attention. It's toxic behavior.
If you have to trick people into caring, you don't actually have a community.
Imagine how they'd feel if they knew you were 'leaning into' it for a text message.
Fix your self-esteem so you don't need a crisis to feel important.
Analyze the time spent on 'sad' theater vs 'improvement' actions. The ROI on theater is negative.
Social capital is a limited resource. You are burning yours for short-term dopamine hits.
Stop the performance. If people leave, then the relationship was based on a false premise.
Your ' invisibility' is actually freedom. Use it to build a real life.
Logic says: Truth is the only way to find out who actually values you.

title: My partner has 'Main Character Syndrome' and I'm just a supporting extra.
content: Every conversation leads back to their day, their stress, their wins. If I have a problem, they listen for two minutes before saying 'That reminds me of when I...' I feel like I'm a prop in their biopic. We’ve been together 3 years and I don’t think they could tell you what my favorite book is or what I’m actually afraid of.

replies.content: bruh, u r basically a NPC in your own house. that's wild.
no cap, start a timer next time u talk. show them the stats. 'u talked for 40 mins, i got 2.'
does your partner even know your birthday at this point? lol.

content: I went through a really messy, public breakup last year. My 'best friend' was there for me, or so I thought. I recently found out that she’s been telling our entire social circle (and even strangers!) my most private, painful stories to make herself look 'deep' or 'supportive.' She literally uses my trauma as an icebreaker at parties. 'Oh, you think that’s bad? My best friend literally found her ex...' I feel like my life is just a script for her social performance.

replies.content: she's a social parasite. she's eating your pain for clout. block her.
if she was your friend, she'd keep your secrets in a vault. she's keeping them in a megaphone.
how many 'likes' did she get on the post about your misery? because that's all she cares about.
stop giving her material. go silent and watch how fast she finds a new 'victim' to support.
she isn't 'deep,' she's just a gossip with a better vocabulary. call it what it is.
bruh, that's high-key toxic. she's clout-chasing on your sadness lol.
imagine being an icebreaker? 'hi i'm stacy and my friend's life is a trainwreck.' yikes.
no cap, that's a main character energy move but in the worst way.
i'd post a story tagging her like 'thanks for sharing my business with everyone!' and see her fold.
drop her bestie. u don't need a PR manager for your trauma.
This is a form of 'secondary victimization.' She is deriving social utility from your distress.
The behavior indicates a lack of empathy and a high need for external validation via 'virtue signaling.'
By positioning herself as the 'helper,' she gains social status without actually having to experience the trauma herself.
This relationship is parasitic, not symbiotic. The emotional cost to you is unsustainable.
Observe: Does she ever discuss HER vulnerabilities, or only yours?
Integrity means keeping a confidence even when it would make you look good to break it.
She is failing the most basic test of friendship: loyalty. You cannot trust her with your heart.
Tell her exactly how her 'sharing' has impacted you. If she gets defensive, you have your answer.
A true friend carries your burdens with you, she doesn't display them like trophies.
Value yourself enough to walk away from people who treat your life like entertainment.
Oh honey, I am so sorry. That must feel like such a huge betrayal of trust.
Maybe she doesn't realize she's doing it? Sometimes people talk without thinking about the hurt they cause.
It's so hard when the person we turn to for comfort becomes the source of our pain.
You deserve to have your stories kept safe. They are yours and yours alone.
I'm sending you a big hug. You are so much more than what happened to you.
You should start making up fake, insane stories and tell her in 'confidence.' See how long it takes to hear them back.
Tell her you've joined a secret society of billionaire mimes. Let’s see her explain that at a party.
If you're her currency, I hope she at least buys you a drink with the 'clout' she’s getting.
Maybe she’s just an aspiring screenwriter and you’re her only source of drama?
I'd charge her a royalty fee for every time she mentions your ex. You'd be rich.
I had a friend like this. She told everyone about my medical issues. I found out when a stranger asked me how my 'surgery' went.
It’s a specific kind of violation. It makes you feel like you’re on a stage you never signed up for.
I cut that person off immediately. The silence was so much better than the exposure.
Real friends don't make your pain about them. Ever.
Don't look back. People like that never change; they just find new 'material.'
The vulnerability you shared was a gift, and she treated it like trash. I'm so sad for you.
You are a soul, not a story. Don't let her define you by your darkest hour.
I hope you find someone who listens with their heart, not their social calendar.
Holding space for you today. You deserve to be heard and respected.
She isn't worth your tears. She's already stolen enough of your light.
Assess the damage to your social reputation. Is she impacting your professional network too?
A 'friend' who leaks information is a security risk. Terminate all data sharing immediately.
Think of your private life as intellectual property. She's infringing on it without a license.
The ROI on this friendship is deeply negative. Cut your losses and pivot to new associates.
Logic says: Silence is the best defense against a gossip.
We are all secrets wrapped in skin. When someone peels that skin back for others to see, they are trying to kill you.
She is building a monument to her own 'kindness' out of the stones of your suffering.
Words are like birds; once they are out of the cage, they never come back. She let your birds go.
Your life is a sacred text. Don't let her be the translator.
The betrayal isn't the telling; it's the fact that she doesn't think you're worth the silence.

title: I’m 'rich' on Instagram and drowning in debt in real life.
content: I have 50k followers. My feed is all luxury travel, designer bags, and 'manifesting my dream life.' The truth is, I have $80k in credit card debt. My car was almost repossessed last month. I’m living in a tiny, moldy studio apartment and taking photos in hotel lobbies I can’t afford to stay in. I’m terrified that if I stop, my entire identity will disappear. I’ve become a ghost in a Gucci belt.

replies.content: you're not a 'ghost,' you're a fraud. and the bill is coming due.
50k followers won't pay for a bankruptcy lawyer. wake up.
the Gucci belt is probably fake anyway, just like the rest of your life.
you're literally ruining your future for likes from people who wouldn't help you if you were on fire.
stop 'manifesting' and start working a second job at a grocery store. at least that's real.
This is a catastrophic financial failure. $80k at 24% APR is a death sentence for your credit.
What is the ROI on 50k followers? If you aren't clearing $10k a month in sponsorships, you are a failing business.
Liquidate the bags. Now. The resale value drops every day you wait.
You are trading long-term security for short-term vanity metrics. It’s an irrational trade.
Declare bankruptcy. It’s the only way to hard-reset the system before you lose everything else.
You are suffering from 'Luxury Dysmorphia,' where your internal self-worth is tied to the perception of external wealth.
The ' Gucci belt' acts as a psychological armor against the reality of your poverty.
Instagram is a feedback loop that rewards the very behavior that is destroying you.
The 'fear of disappearance' is a sign that you have fully merged your identity with your digital avatar.
Delete the app. Your nervous system cannot handle the cognitive dissonance much longer.
bruh, 80k in debt? that's not 'manifesting,' that's just a bad credit score lol.
imagine taking pics in a lobby and then going home to mold? that's a wild movie plot.
no cap, just come clean. 'the transition to being broke' content goes viral these days.
vibes are so low here. get a job that pays in cash bruh.
ur followers don't care about u, they just want to see pretty stuff. don't die for them.
Oh honey, you must be so exhausted. Carrying a secret that big is so heavy.
It's okay to be normal! You don't have to be a superstar to be loved.
I promise you, the people who really love you won't care about the bags.
Please talk to a financial advisor or even your parents. Don't hide in that moldy room alone.
You are a precious human being, not a brand. Sending you so much love.
Can I borrow $10? Wait, never mind. I’ll buy you a coffee, you clearly need it.
Is 'ghost in a Gucci belt' your new aesthetic? It’s very avant-garde.
Just start an OnlyFans. At least then people are paying for the performance.
I manifests a pizza every Friday and I still have to pay for it. Life is hard.
If you go to jail for fraud, make sure to take some 'prison chic' photos before they take your phone.
Integrity is the only thing that will save you. You are living a lie, and it's eating your soul.
Confess to your followers. Tell the truth. Use your platform to warn others about this trap.
Character is built in the valleys, not on the fake mountain tops of Instagram.
Every fake post is a brick in the wall between you and a real life. Stop building it.
You are better than this. Be a woman of truth.
The glitter you've been throwing is just ground-up glass. It's cutting you every time you touch it.
You are a prisoner of a dream you no longer want to have. Wake up.
The mold in your room is more real than the filters on your face. Listen to the rot.
We are all chasing shadows, but you have chained yourself to yours.
When you have nothing left to lose, you will finally find out who is actually standing there.
I went through this. I lost everything, including my 'friends.' It was the best thing that ever happened to me.
The relief of not lying anymore is better than any designer bag. I promise.
You are in survival mode. Your brain is fried. Take a break from the screen.
Sell the car. Get a bus pass. Reclaim your sanity.
One day at a time. Start by telling one person the truth today.
My heart breaks for the loneliness you must feel in the middle of all those 'likes.'
You are trying to fill a hole in your heart with things that don't fit. It's okay to stop.
You are worthy of a real, messy, debt-free life. Don't let the algorithm kill you.
Holding space for the real you—the one who is scared and tired.
Turn off the phone and just breathe. You are enough without the Gucci.

title: I’m the 'successful' child in the abroad, but I’m one missed paycheck away from homelessness.
content: My family back home thinks I’m swimming in dollars. I send 40% of my salary home every month for my brother’s school fees and my mom’s 'business' that never starts. Meanwhile, I’m eating 0.50p noodles in a cold room in London and I haven't bought new shoes in two years. I can’t tell them I’m struggling because it will 'kill their spirit,' but I’m literally drowning in the 'Black Tax.'

replies.content: you're not a hero, you're a victim of your own silence. stop sending the money or you'll be the one they're 'praying for' when you're on the street.
nigerian families and 'businesses' that never start... name a more iconic duo. they're eating your life.
if you can't afford shoes, you can't afford to be a philanthropist. period.
Run the numbers. If you lose your job, can your family support you? No. Then you are being financially irresponsible to yourself.
You are subsidizing a lifestyle they haven't earned with a life you haven't built yet.
Logic says: Save yourself first, or eventually, everyone sinks.
no cap, the japa life is a scam if u r just a glorified ATM. tell them things are 'hard' too.
everyone thinks abroad is paved with gold lol. show them your bank statement and watch them ghost u.
Oh my dear, the pressure to provide is so heavy. But you must be kind to yourself too.
God will provide, but please don't starve yourself for people who can work.
This is cultural guilt-tripping masquerading as filial piety. It is a drain on your upward mobility.
Establish a fixed remittance limit. Anything above that is a threat to your survival.
Next time they ask, tell them the UK government has started taxing 'sent money' at 90%.
I told my family I'm a professional 'pigeon feeder' now. They stopped asking for money real quick.
Honesty is a mercy. If they knew the truth, and they still asked, then you'd know where you stand.
I stopped sending money for a year and my family actually survived. They just found other ways.
They are using you to keep up appearances in the village while you are dying in private.
I feel this. My dad asked for a new car while I was literally walking to work in the snow.
send them a photo of your '0.50p noodles.' see if it tastes as good to them.
you're enabling their laziness. the 'business' isn't starting because your salary is the business.
You are such a good child, but even Jesus rested. You need to rest too.
Sending prayers for your breakthrough. You will not lack!
An ATM doesn't have feelings, but you do. Stop operating like a machine.
Black Tax is a liability. Your savings account is an asset. Prioritize the asset.
bruh, London is too cold to be broke. don't play yourself.
if they want dollars, tell them to go to Binance like everyone else.
The psychological toll of 'keeping up appearances' is higher than the financial cost.
Remittance culture is a barrier to generational wealth. Break the cycle.
Tell them you've become a monk and given away all your worldly possessions.
I once sent my mom a picture of a bill instead of money. She didn't reply for a week.
You are teaching them that your labor is free. It is not.
The truth will set you free, but first, it will make everyone in the village angry.
Boundary setting is a skill. Practice saying 'No' without an explanation.
You are more than a paycheck. If they don't see that, they don't see you.
The moment I stopped the 'money flow,' I found out who actually loved me. Spoiler: it was only 2 people.
Your future is being sacrificed for their present comfort. That is a bad deal.
I literally cried at the grocery store today because I couldn't afford cheese. Cheese!
Being a 'Big Boy' abroad is the biggest lie we tell ourselves.
Did you check if your mom actually has a shop? Some moms just give the money to the church.
Ask for receipts. Every time. The requests will slow down.
I moved back to Lagos because being poor in London was more expensive than being poor in Gbagada.
The shame of 'failing' abroad is real, but the shame of being 50 with zero savings is worse.
You are a bird trying to fly with a whole mountain on your wings.
The sea between you and home is full of the tears of people who 'made it.'
I'm sending you so much warmth. Please buy yourself a warm meal today. You earned it.
You are not a bad person for wanting to survive.

title: My fiancé wants a 10-million naira wedding, but we have 200k in the bank.
content: He says we have to 'do it for the culture' and that his family will be embarrassed if we don't have a huge hall in Victoria Island with 500 guests. He wants to take a loan from a microfinance bank to cover it. I told him we should just do a small court wedding and a lunch, but he says I'm 'bringing him down.' I’m terrified of starting a marriage in debt just to feed people who will complain about the jollof rice anyway.

replies.content: if he takes that loan, he's a fool. if you marry him while he does it, you're a bigger one.
the 'culture' doesn't pay interest on microfinance loans. but you will for the next 5 years.
500 guests? 450 of them are just there to criticize the souvenir and the meat size.
A 10m wedding on a 200k budget is a 5000% deficit. This isn't a wedding, it's a financial suicide pact.
Loans for consumption are the fastest way to poverty. Marriage is a partnership, not a theatrical production.
If his family is embarrassed, let THEM pay the 10 million. Problem solved.
bruh, VI hall for 500 people? is he a politician? lol.
the jollof will definitely be dry and people will still talk rubbish on the way home. no cap.
Oh sugar, a marriage is about the two of you, not the party! Please don't start with debt.
Try to talk to his mother? Maybe she can talk some sense into him?
This is a classic 'prestige trap.' He is prioritizing social signaling over economic stability.
The stress of debt is the leading cause of early marital friction. The data is clear.
Just tell everyone the wedding is 'strictly by invitation' and then only invite the 200k worth of people.
10 million naira could buy enough gala and coke to feed the whole of Lagos. Just saying.
Character is refusing to live a lie. If you don't have 10m, don't spend 10m. Simple.
My cousin did this. They are still paying the loan and they've been divorced for 2 years.
The pressure to 'show off' in Nigeria is a mental illness. Don't catch it.
Check the interest rate on that microfinance loan. It's probably 10% a MONTH. You will die.
if he cares more about 'people' than your future, he doesn't love you. he loves his ego.
cancel the hall. buy a plot of land. tell his family to eat the grass.
The opportunity cost of 10m is a down payment on a house or a solid investment portfolio.
Starting a life at -10,000,000 is a statistical failure waiting to happen.
even the small chops will be small for that price lol. just do registry bruh.
if i'm a guest, i'm just there for the pounded yam. i don't care about your debt.
Is he trying to impress his ex? Or just the 'boys' at the club?
Performative wealth is the enemy of actual wealth.
Tell him you're allergic to 'large gatherings' and the only cure is a small lunch.
Maybe the guests can pay an entry fee? Call it 'Agbada Tax.'
A man who wants to borrow for a party is not a man who can protect a home.
The Bible says 'Owe no man anything.' Remind him of that since he likes 'culture.'
I'm 100% serious: don't marry him until he sees reason. This is a red flag the size of Nigeria.
He's not 'doing it for the culture,' he's doing it because he's insecure.
Ask him for a breakdown of the 10m. Watch him struggle to justify 2m for 'decor.'
If you sign that loan paper, you are signing your own warrant.
Peace of mind is better than a gold-plated cake. I promise.
I tried to explain the math and he said I'm 'acting like a man.' I'm just acting like someone who wants to eat next year!
I think I’m going to tell him the wedding is off if he takes that loan.
A palace built on sand will fall, but a tent built on rock will stand the storm.
Don't let the noise of the crowd drown out the voice of your wisdom.
Nigeria is the only place where you invite 500 people and 700 show up. Plan for 1000 or don't plan at all.
Do a morning wedding and serve breakfast. People hate breakfast weddings. They won't come. Problem solved.
I did the 'big wedding' thing. We fought about the bills for the first three years. Not worth it.
The 'embarrassment' of a small wedding is temporary. The 'embarrassment' of a car being seized is permanent.
Stand your ground. You are the one who will have to manage the 'home budget' later.

title: My 'Pastor' just asked me to donate my rent money as a 'seed' for a miracle.
content: I’ve been going to this church for three years. I lost my job last month and I’m struggling. The Pastor called me into his office and said he 'saw a vision' that if I give my last 150k (which is my rent for the next quarter) as a seed, God will give me a 1.5 million naira job by Friday. I want to believe, but my landlord is not a 'spirit' and he doesn't take 'amen' as payment. Am I being faithless or am I being scammed?

replies.content: you're being scammed by a man in a shiny suit. if he's so sure about the miracle, ask him to pay your rent and take the 1.5m when it comes.
pastors like this are why people are leaving the church. they're just spiritual yahoo boys.
if you give that money, you're not 'sowing a seed,' you're 'buying a tent' for yourself on the street.
bruh, your pastor is playing 4D chess with your life lol. 150k for a 'vision'?
tell him to sow HIS car as a seed for your job. let's see how much faith he has.
Oh dear, God wants us to be wise! He gave us a brain for a reason.
A real pastor would be helping you find a job, not taking your last kobo.
This is a psychological exploitation technique known as 'predatory spirituality.' It targets those in a state of high stress.
The 'vision' is a non-falsifiable claim designed to bypass your logical defenses. Ignore it.
The probability of a 1000% return on investment by Friday is zero. This is a bad financial move.
Keep your rent. A roof over your head is a guaranteed asset. The 'seed' is a total loss.
God is not a gambler. He doesn't need your rent money to bless you. This man is a wolf.
Maybe the 'miracle' is you finding a better church? That would be worth the 150k.
I did this once. I ended up living in my sister's parlor for six months. Don't do it.
Notice how the Pastor never 'sees a vision' that he should give YOU money? Funny that.
Nigerians and 'miracles'... we will rather pray for a job than update our CV. Pay your rent, friend.
he's probably going to use your 150k to fuel his SUV. that's the only miracle happening here.
if you give him that money, don't come here to cry when the landlord throws your 'seed' out on the road.
The Bible says God loves a cheerful giver, but He also says to provide for your own household.
I'll pray for you to find a real job, one that doesn't require a down payment to God.
The 'Pastor' is a middleman who is taking a 100% commission on your faith.
Logic says: Pay the landlord. He is the one with the legal right to evict you, not the spirit.
no cap, some churches are just business centers with better music lol.
if friday comes and no job, will the pastor refund u? ask him that. watch him stutter.
High-control religious environments often use financial depletion to increase dependency on the group.
Protect your capital. You are in a state of economic vulnerability.
Tell the Pastor you had a vision too—a vision of you paying your rent on time.
Miracles are free. Scams have a 150k entry fee.
You are being tested, yes. But the test is whether you have the wisdom to see a thief in a pulpit.
True faith doesn't ask you to be reckless with your survival.
The 'vision' is always about money. Never about you finding peace or healing.
Run from that church. If you stay, they will take everything until you have nothing left to give.
Did you check the Pastor's shoes? I bet they cost more than your rent.
He's not a man of God, he's a man of your pocket.
The altar is not a betting shop. God is not a bookie.
Faith is a bridge, but you are trying to walk on a shadow.
I worked for a guy like this once. He called his bank accounts 'Heavenly Portals.'
Tell him you already 'seeded' the money to your landlord as a sacrifice for a peaceful home.
Religion in Nigeria is a very lucrative industry. Don't be the product.
If you want a 1.5m job, send out 150 CVs instead of 150k naira.

title: I’m 30, single, and my mother has started adding my name to 'marriage prayer' lists at every church in the state.
content: Every time I call home, the first thing she asks is if I've met a 'responsible man.' Last week, she sent me a photo of a prayer point list from a mountain where she spent three days fasting for my 'settlement.' I have a great career, I just bought a car, and I’m actually happy. But her constant pity is making me feel like a failed project. She even suggested I should 'dress more like a wife' to attract the right person. I’m tired.

replies.content: bruh, 'dress like a wife' is crazy. does that mean wearing an apron to the club? lol.
no cap, nigerian moms think 30 is 100. they are living in 1950.
Oh honey, she just wants to see you settled! It comes from a place of love, even if it's annoying.
Maybe just go on one date she suggests? Just to make her happy?
don't listen to User_02. if you give her an inch, she'll bring a wedding planner to your house next week.
you're not a 'failed project,' your mom just has no hobbies besides monitoring your womb.
This is 'societal timeline pressure' internalized by the parent and projected onto the child. It is toxic.
Your success (car, career) is being devalued because it doesn't fit the patriarchal 'success' model of marriage.
Integrity is being happy in your own skin regardless of your marital status. Don't let her dim your light.
My mom did this until I told her I was moving to another country. Then she started praying for my 'safety' instead.
Start sending HER prayer points. 'Prayer for my mother to mind her business.' See how she likes it.
I'm 28 and my mom already bought the Aso-Ebi for a wedding that doesn't exist. Help me.
The 'mountain' fasting is the final boss of Nigerian mom pressure. Good luck.
Ask her why she's so eager to send you to another man's house? Is she tired of you? (Use guilt back!).
being single and rich is better than being married and miserable. tell her that every day.
if she wants a wedding so bad, she should renew her own vows and leave you alone.
A good husband is a blessing! Don't be so closed off to the idea, sweetie.
I'll add you to my prayer list too! (For happiness, not just marriage!).
imagine being at the office and your mom is on a mountain screaming your name lol. vibes are crazy.
just tell her u r dating a ghost. she'll stop praying and start calling the herbalist.
The 'settlement' narrative implies that a woman is 'unsettled' or 'homeless' without a husband. It's a linguistic trap.
Focus on your financial autonomy. It is the only thing that actually protects you.
Tell her you've decided to become a nun. The church prayers will get very confusing after that.
Nigerian moms think 'husband' is a job title. It's not.
You are a whole person, not a half waiting for a completion. Stand firm.
If God wanted you married by Friday, you'd be married. Tell her to take it up with Him.
The pity is the worst part. They look at you like you have a terminal illness just because you're single.
I cut my mom off for 3 months because of this. She finally learned to talk about other things.
My mom told me my 'big career' is scaring men away. Good! I want a man who isn't easily scared.
We should start a 'Single & Happy' Aso-Ebi club.
You are a garden that is already in bloom. You don't need a fence to be beautiful.
The mountain she climbed is made of her own fears, not your needs.
I just want to eat my jollof rice in peace without being asked who cooked it. Is that too much to ask?
The next person who says 'You're next' at a wedding is getting a slap. Honestly.
Enjoy your car and your freedom. A husband can't be parked in the garage when he annoys you.

title: My husband’s younger brother has been 'visiting' for 8 months and he refuses to leave.
content: He arrived with one small bag for a 'two-week stay' to look for a job. Now his boxes are arriving from the village. He eats all the food, uses the AC 24/7, and brings girls home when we are at work. My husband says 'he is my blood, I can’t throw him out,' but I’m the one paying the electricity bills and doing the grocery shopping. I feel like a tenant in my own house while he’s the landlord. The 'Extended Family' system is killing my marriage.

replies.content: the brother is a squatter and your husband is his enabler. throw both of them out and change the locks.
'he is my blood' is the favorite excuse of weak men who can't lead their homes. he's disrespecting you.
stop buying food. eat out. let him find an empty fridge for a week and see if he stays.
bruh, 8 months? that's not a visit, that's an occupation lol.
no cap, the girls coming over is the wildest part. he thinks he's in a hotel.
Oh dear, family is important but there must be limits! Have you tried talking to him nicely?
Maybe help him find a small room somewhere else? Pay the first month's rent just to get him out?
From a financial perspective, he is a 'parasitic drain' on your household assets. He has zero utility.
The AC usage alone is probably costing you an extra 20k a month. Cut the power cord.
This is a boundary failure. In many cultures, 'family' is used as a weapon to bypass individual rights.
Your husband is experiencing 'conflict avoidance.' He would rather you be unhappy than his brother be inconvenienced.
Honesty: Tell your husband that if the brother doesn't leave by Saturday, you are leaving until he does.
Start charging him for the AC. Put a coin-operated meter on his bedroom door.
I lived through this. I ended up packing my bags and going to my mother's house. My husband learned his lesson in 3 days.
Nigerians and 'brotherhood'... they will let their wife suffer to please a lazy relative. It’s a shame.
Does he have a job yet? If not, he’s not looking. He’s just enjoying the free life.
the 'blood' excuse ends where the bills begin. he's a grown man, not a baby.
if he brings a girl over again, walk in and ask her for her share of the rent. watch her run.
Maybe pray for him to find a good job so he can be independent? God can move him!
I'm so sorry you're going through this. A home should be a sanctuary.
If you are the one paying the bills, YOU are the head of that household financially. Act like it.
The cost of 'peace' in this situation is your long-term retirement savings. It's too high.
bruh, tell him the house is haunted lol. move his stuff to the balcony and see what happens.
if your husband won't step up, u gotta be the bad guy. someone has to do it.
The 'Extended Family' system is only sustainable if all members contribute. He is a 'free rider.'
Negotiate a 'hard exit date' with your husband. No extensions.
Start playing 'traditional music' at 4 AM every morning. If he wants a village life, give it to him.
I'd 'accidentally' spill something really smelly in his room. Like fermented locust beans.
A man's first priority is his wife, not his siblings. Your husband is failing his vows.
Be firm. Love doesn't mean being a doormat for a lazy relative.
The moment he brought girls into your marital home, he lost any right to 'respect.' Kick him out.
If your husband chooses him over you, you know where you stand in his heart.
I'm going to start taking the router with me to work. No more free data for him.
I've decided. Sunday is the deadline. I don't care who is 'blood.'
Nigerian in-laws can be the worst. They act like they own your life because they 'gave' you their son.
Tell him his mother called and said she needs him in the village immediately for a 'land issue.' He'll be gone in an hour.

title: My boss at my Lagos firm hasn't paid us in 3 months, but he just bought a new G-Wagon.
content: He calls us into the office every Monday for 'motivation' and tells us to 'sacrifice for the vision.' He says the company is 'passing through a phase' because of the exchange rate. But on Saturday, I saw him on Instagram at a club in VI spraying money and showing off a new 2024 G-Wagon. I’m broke, I’m trekking to work, and he’s telling me to 'believe in the brand.' How do I get my money without getting blacklisted in the industry?

replies.content: his 'vision' is using your sweat to fuel his car. stop trekking to a job that doesn't pay you. you're a volunteer, not an employee.
The ROI of your time is currently negative. You are literally subsidizing his luxury with your poverty.
bruh, 'sacrifice for the vision' is the biggest scam in Lagos lol. he's wildin.
This is a classic 'narcissistic leadership' model. He views employees as tools for his personal 'Senior Man' status.
A man who owes wages while living in luxury has no integrity. You cannot build a career on a rotten foundation.
Ask him if the G-Wagon runs on 'visions' or if he uses fuel. Since he thinks you can live on air.
Gather your colleagues. If everyone stops coming, the 'vision' will stop moving real fast.
I worked for a guy like this in Lekki. When I quit, he tried to sue me. Don't be scared, he's a coward.
Lagos bosses will tell you 'we are a family' so they can treat you like a houseboy. Leave now.
He is building his mountain on your shadows. Move, and let him fall.
screenshot the Instagram posts. keep them as 'motivation' for when you report him to the labor ministry.
Audit the company if you can. He's likely diverting operational funds for personal assets. That's a crime.
next time he asks for a report, send him a picture of the G-Wagon tires. no cap.
The motivational speeches are a gaslighting technique to keep you from demanding your legal rights.
Oh dear, God will provide a better job for you. But please, don't suffer in silence.
Is the G-Wagon bulletproof? Because he's shooting himself in the foot with this behavior.
I bet he still expects you to come early and stay late. The audacity of Nigerian bosses.
Stop doing any work. Just show up, sit down, and use their Wi-Fi to apply for new jobs.
If you are trekking to work, you are already blacklisted from having a good life by this man.
Tell him your 'sacrifice' has reached its limit and now you need 'salvation' in Naira.
if he can spray money, he can pay salaries. he just doesn't respect you.
If you don't act, you are setting a precedent that your labor is free. It is not.
I hope the G-Wagon develops a mechanical fault in the middle of Third Mainland Bridge.
His 'Senior Man' complex is funded by your hunger. That is a moral failure.
Maybe talk to the other staff? If you all speak together, he might listen.
Ask for a ride in the G-Wagon since you're the one who technically paid for it.
The 'vision' is blurred by greed. It's time to find a new lens.
Nigerian labor laws are weak, but social media is strong. Tag him on Twitter.
I left a job like this and my blood pressure dropped instantly. No money is worth your health.
The G-Wagon will rust, but the debt he owes you will remain in the heavens.
threaten to tag the car dealer in his 'vision' posts. watch how fast he finds your 3 months' pay.
Logic says: Silence is consent. If you don't demand it, he assumes you don't need it.
Lagos life is hard enough without being scammed by your own boss. shege pro max.
Is the AC in the G-Wagon cold? Because your pocket is currently freezing.
Start a 'work-to-rule.' Do the absolute bare minimum until the alerts start hitting.
I feel for you. I’m also waiting for 2 months salary. These bosses have no conscience.
The 'hustle' is real, but this is just pure wickedness.
If you quit today, will he even notice? Or will he just hire another 'sacrifice'?
Don't worry about being 'blacklisted.' Most good companies know who the bad bosses are.
A 'G-Wagon' on empty pockets. The irony of the Nigerian elite.
if he asks for a meeting, tell him your 'network' is down because you couldn't pay for data.
Value your labor. If he doesn't, nobody else will.
next time he talks about 'sacrifice,' ask him for a loan to buy gala. lol.
The exploitation of 'youthful energy' is a pillar of the Lagos corporate world.
I hope he sprays fake money next time he's at the club.
Character is revealed in how a man treats those who can do nothing for him.
Go to the office with a plate and ask for your portion of the 'vision.'
Pack your bags and leave. A better day is coming.
Imagine spraying money when your staff are drinking garri. Hell is real.
The road you trek is the path to your freedom from this man.

title: I’m the 'First Born' son and I feel like I’m the parent of my own parents.
content: I’m 32. My dad retired early and refused to invest, my mom’s shop 'failed' for the fifth time. I have 4 younger siblings. I pay for everyone’s school fees, rent, and even my dad’s blood pressure meds. I want to marry my girlfriend of 4 years, but I can’t afford a ring because I’m paying for my brother’s final year project. I feel like my life hasn't started because I’m busy sustaining theirs. Is this what being a 'Senior Man' means?

replies.content: The 'First Born' burden in Nigeria is a heavy cross. You are carrying a whole village on your back.
Bless you, son. God sees your sacrifice! But please, don't lose your woman over this.
you're not a 'Senior Man,' you're a safety net. and they're jumping on you because they know you won't break.
You are experiencing 'familial enmeshment.' You have lost the boundary between your life and theirs.
bruh, 4 years? if u don't marry that girl, another man will. and he won't be paying for your brother's project.
Honesty: Sit them down and show them the ledger. Let them see the weight you are carrying.
Tell your brother to use ChatGPT for his project and save you some money. (Kidding, or am I?).
You are hindering your siblings' growth. By solving every problem, you are making them useless.
My brother did this for us. Now he's 45, single, and bitter. Don't be like him.
Does your girlfriend know the full extent of the bills? She needs to know what she's marrying into.
It's okay to tell your siblings to get part-time jobs. You are not their God.
Ask your mother to try a different business, maybe something smaller?
let your dad find a hobby that pays. stop being the retirement plan he forgot to buy.
If you don't set a limit, you will wake up at 50 with no family of your own and a lot of 'thank you' notes.
no cap, tell your siblings to start a side hustle. they are too comfortable.
I'm the first daughter, so I know this pain. The 'Senior Man' title is a scam.
The school fees for 4 siblings? Are you a billionaire? You need to cut some off.
Your parents are effectively 'infantilizing' you by making you the provider for everything.
Being a good son is different from being a victim. Draw the line.
I hope your brother appreciates that project. Some siblings are just ungrateful.
Allocate a fixed percentage of your income to them. Anything extra is a no.
if your girl loves you, she will wait. but don't make her wait forever lol.
if the shop 'failed' 5 times, she's not a business woman. she's a hobbyist. stop funding it.
God will replenish your pockets! But save some for the wedding too.
Financial boundaries are an act of love, not rejection. Remember that.
Start telling them your salary was cut. See who still calls you 'Senior Man.'
Send them memes about 'Black Tax.' Maybe they'll take the hint.
I am praying for your breakthrough. You deserve a life too.
The 'First Born' complex is why so many Nigerians are depressed but silent.
Don't let them eat your future. You are not a bank.
If you don't marry that girl this year, I will marry her for you. Stop wasting time!
Ask your dad why he retired early without a plan. Have that hard conversation.
Your brother should be doing 'side hustles' to help with his project.
I feel like I'm reading my own diary. Stay strong, brother.
You are a bridge that everyone is walking on. Eventually, the bridge needs repairs.
if you buy that ring, your mom will ask why you didn't use the money for a new freezer. you can't win.
Prioritize your own house. You cannot pour from an empty cup.
first born life is a setup lol. u get the most beatings and the most bills.
The 'culture' of sacrifice is often just a culture of exploitation.
Your siblings need to feel the 'heat' of the economy. Stop cooling it for them.
Maybe move to another city? 'Out of sight, out of pocket.'
Your girlfriend sounds like a saint for waiting 4 years. Reward her.
The 'Senior Man' title doesn't pay for a honeymoon in Zanzibar.
I stopped sending money for a month and my family suddenly found 'hidden' savings. Try it.
You are not responsible for your parents' poor financial decisions.
Lagos is too expensive to be a philanthropist. Focus on yourself.
I hope your siblings get jobs and pay you back one day. (They probably won't).
Take a deep breath. You are doing great, but you need to stop.
The sun shines for everyone, not just those who carry the clouds. Let them feel the sun too.
Thanks everyone. I think I’m going to have that 'budget' meeting tonight. Wish me luck.

title: My husband wants a second wife because I haven't 'given' him a son.
content: We have three beautiful daughters. I had complications during the last birth and the doctor said I shouldn't try again. Now my husband says his 'lineage' will end with him and his mother is already scouting for a 'strong village girl' to bring to Lagos. I’ve built this home with him for 12 years. I’m a partner at my law firm, but in this house, I’m just a 'failed' incubator. What happened to our love?

replies.content: the 'lineage' excuse is just a cover for him wanting a younger model. take your law degree and sue him for everything.
A man who devalues his daughters is not a man of God or character. He is a man of ego.
Oh my sister, this is so painful. Men and their pride... it's a terrible thing.
This is 'genetic narcissism.' He views his children as extensions of himself rather than individuals.
bruh, 2026 and people are still pressed about sons? your daughters will probably be the ones taking care of him anyway lol.
Don't accept the 'village girl' in your house. Once she enters, your peace is gone forever.
As a lawyer, you know the legal implications of a second marriage under the Act. Use your knowledge.
This is why I'm scared of marrying into 'traditional' families. The pressure never ends.
He is looking for a ghost of himself in the future, and ignoring the real life standing in front of him.
Tell him if he brings a second wife, you'll bring a second husband. Equal rights and all that.
if he wants a 'strong village girl,' let him go and live in the village. see if she can help him with his law firm bills.
You are a daughter of the Most High. You are not a 'failure.' Stand in your truth.
Pray for his heart to change. But also, protect your daughters from this mindset.
Biologically, the male determines the sex of the child. If he wants to blame someone, he should look in the mirror.
tell him to go and adopt. oh wait, he wants 'blood.' some people are just backwards no cap.
The 'mother-in-law' factor is always the catalyst for this drama. She needs to mind her business.
Three daughters? That's a house full of blessings. He is blind.
In 20 years, those daughters will be the ones buying him his BP meds while the 'son' is busy being a brat.
His 'lineage' isn't that important. He's not the Oba of Lagos.
Stand your ground. If you allow this, you are teaching your daughters that they are 'lesser.'
I left a marriage for this exact reason. I’m happier now with my two girls.
Is he even contributing to the girls' lives? Or is he just obsessed with a penis?
if he brings the girl, pack your bags and move to your own house. you're a partner at a law firm, you don't need him.
The 'Act' marriage protects you from polygamy. Remind him of the jail time.
Patriarchy is a poison that destroys even the most successful homes.
My dad did this. The second wife was a nightmare and she never even had a son either. Karma.
Men like this don't deserve the women they have.
Tell him to go to a fertility clinic. Maybe the issue is him.
I feel so small in this house right now. Thank you for the support.
You are a queen. Don't let a man who thinks in the 18th century tell you otherwise.
The 'village girl' will eventually want his properties too. He's making a mistake.
Lagos is full of single successful women. You won't be alone.
His mother should have stayed in the village if she wants village rules.
A son doesn't guarantee a legacy. Character does.
Your daughters are watching how you handle this. Show them strength.
Don't cry for a man who doesn't see your value.
Polygamy in a modern home is a recipe for disaster.
He's throwing away 12 years for a 'possibility.' He's a fool.
The stars don't care if they are male or female, they just shine. Your girls are stars.
ask him if he has the money to maintain two households in this economy. fuel price alone will finish him.
Maybe talk to your father-in-law? Sometimes they are more reasonable.
File for a legal separation if he goes through with it. Protect your assets.
imagine being a law partner and dealing with this. the world is wild lol.
He is prioritizing a biological desire over a marital commitment.
His daughters will resent him forever for this.
A son can also be a 'prodigal son.' There are no guarantees.
Tell him you'll name the next dog after his lineage.
True love is sacrificial. He is being the opposite.
Stay strong, counsel. You have the law and the truth on your side.
I hope you find peace, whether with him or without him.

title: I lied to my friends that I got a job at a 'Big Four' firm, and now they want me to 'wash' it.
content: I’ve been unemployed for a year. The pressure was too much, so when they asked, I lied and said I got a job at KPMG. Now they are planning a 'celebration' dinner and expect me to pay for the first round of drinks and 'wash' the new job. I’m currently down to my last 5k and I’m terrified. I have to show up on Monday at an office I don't work at. How do I stop this lie before it ruins me?

replies.content: bruh, 'washing' a job u don't have is the ultimate Lagos L. how r u gonna pay for the Moët? lol.
you're a clown. the 'washing' culture is stupid anyway, but doing it with 5k is insane.
Tell them you 'lost the offer' because of a background check on your social media. It sounds believable.
This is 'performative competence.' You are more afraid of social shame than financial ruin.
The truth is a heavy lift, but a lie is a permanent weight. Tell them today.
The 'Big Four' will find out if you keep using their name. Don't add 'impersonation' to your resume.
Oh sugar, we all want to make our friends proud. But lying won't bring the blessing.
I did this once with a 'fake' promotion. The stress made me lose 5kg in a week. Not worth it.
Cancel the dinner. Say you have 'training' all weekend. Then use that time to find a REAL job.
You are dressed in a suit made of paper. Don't go out in the rain.
just tell them u 'resigned' on the first day because of 'toxic vibes.' no cap.
come clean. tell them you're broke and desperate. if they're real friends, they'll buy YOU dinner.
Or just fake a 'faint' at the dinner when the bill comes. Classic.
The 'wash' culture is why many Nigerians stay poor. We celebrate before we even work.
How were you planning to show up at the office? Standing outside the gate?
The shame of being caught is worse than the shame of being unemployed. Tell them now.
Lagos is full of people living this exact lie. You are not alone, but you are wrong.
Tell them the HR called and said the position was 'put on hold' due to budget cuts.
Your friends will understand if they are truly your friends.
Don't spend that 5k on drinks. That's your transport money for real interviews.
Ethically, you are in a compromised position. Pivot to honesty immediately.
lol imagine being at the bar and the card says 'insufficient funds.' the real shege.
if you go to that dinner, you're a masochist. just block them and find a job.
I'll pray for a real job at KPMG for you! But tell the truth first.
Lying is a coping mechanism for the trauma of rejection. Seek help for the anxiety.
Social media has made us all feel like we are falling behind. It's a trap.
Did you even apply to KPMG? If not, the lie is even deeper.
Say you got a better offer in another city and you're moving. Double down or quit.
My heart goes out to you. Being jobless in Lagos is a special kind of hell.
Humility is the only cure for this. Swallow your pride.
I once lied about my age to get a girl. When the truth came out, I lost everything.
Imagine if one of your friends actually works at KPMG? You're finished.
The 'wash' expectation is so toxic. We need to stop it.
You are 30. You should know better than to lie about your source of income.
I’m typing this while crying. I just wanted to feel important for once.
You ARE important without the job. Realize that.
Maybe this is the motivation you need to actually get the job?
Just say 'I was joking' and hope they laugh. (They won't).
Don't let Lagos 'packaging' kill you. Stay real.
The shadow of a lie is longer than the light of the truth.
if you need 5k for food, ask. don't lie about being a consultant.
Financial planning starts with accurate data. Your data is currently 100% false.
next time, say u got a job at 'The Sun' and then say 'it's too hot to talk about.' lol.
The psychological toll of 'keeping up with the Joneses' (or the Okonkwos) is immense.
Lies are like debt; they eventually come due with interest.
Just tell them you were scammed by a fake recruiter. Everyone in Nigeria understands that.
You'll be fine. Just tell them. A year from now, you'll laugh about it.
The truth will set you free, but first, it will make you very embarrassed.
Why are your friends so eager to eat your money? That's the real question.
I hope you actually get a job soon. For real this time.

title: I found out my 'mentor' is stealing my side-hustle ideas and pitching them to investors.
content: I’m an intern at a tech hub in Yaba. I’ve been sharing my app ideas with my mentor because I thought he was helping me refine them. Today, I saw a press release about a 'new startup' he just launched with $50k seed funding. It’s my EXACT idea, down to the name and the UI colors. He hasn't replied to my messages since the news broke. I have no contract, just WhatsApp chats. Can I still fight this?

replies.content: WhatsApp chats are legally binding evidence of 'intellectual property disclosure' in some contexts. Save the export file immediately.
yaba tech bros are just yahoo boys with Macbooks. don't ever share your 'gold' with a 'mentor' without an NDA.
bruh, he did u dirty. 'refine the idea' means 'let me see how to steal it' lol.
This is 'idea poaching.' He leveraged his higher social capital to monetize your intellectual labor.
Justice is worth fighting for. Do not let him build a house on your stolen bricks.
Apply for a job at his new startup and then quit on the first day with all his passwords. (Don't actually do this).
This is why I don't talk to anyone about my 'next move.' Nigeria will show you shege.
The investors will hate the drama. Threatening a public call-out is your strongest leverage right now.
I’m so sorry. Yaba is full of sharks. I hope you get your credit.
The seed he stole will only grow fruit that tastes of his betrayal. But you still need to eat. Fight him.
Contact a copyright lawyer. $50k is enough to sue for, but he'll likely settle to avoid bad PR.
blast him on Twitter/X. tag the investors. let the world know he's a thief.
vultures in hoodies. stay safe out there in Yaba no cap.
The 'mentor' label provided the psychological safety for you to drop your guard. It's a predatory tactic.
God is the ultimate judge! He will reward your creativity in other ways.
I know that guy! He's always 'looking for young talent' to exploit. Disgusting.
Yaba is turning into a hub for scams, not just tech. It's sad.
Did he even change the name? That's just lazy theft.
If you have the chats, you have the proof. Don't back down.
Investors hate 'founder disputes.' One email to them could freeze his funding.
Never trust anyone who calls themselves a 'Guru.'
The tech world is small. This will follow him forever if you make it loud enough.
Is there a 'Tech Lagos' group? Post it there with receipts.
next time, use a timestamping service for your ideas before sharing them.
The 'Equity' he holds is built on theft. It is inherently unstable.
lol he really thought he could just ghost u? the audacity.
Collective action: Inform other interns at that hub. Protect them.
I’m literally shaking. I spent 6 months on those wireframes.
Maybe he'll give you a 'Consultant' role to shut you up? Take the money then quit.
A name built on a lie will not stand the test of time.
This happens so much in the Nigerian creative space. It's heartbreaking.
Did you sign any intern agreement? Check if it has an 'IP' clause.
The Nigerian legal system is slow, but social media is 5G. Use it.
Shame on him. A mentor should be a ladder, not a thief.
Don't stop being creative, just stop being naive. Lesson learned.
He'll fail eventually because he doesn't understand the 'Why' behind the idea.
I can help you with a legal draft if you want. No charge.
Is the startup already on the App Store? Report it for IP infringement.
Lagos tech is 90% packaging and 10% coding. He's a packaging pro.
Rivers only flow forward. Your next idea will be even better.
if he doesn't reply by tonight, start the thread on Twitter at 8am tomorrow.
Document the date and time of every message you sent him.
imagine if the app crashes on the first day. that would be poetic. lol.
Mentorship should be a safe harbor, not a hunting ground.
I bet he's already planning to 'sell' the company in a year. Fast cash.
Send him a 'Congratulations' message with a link to your lawyer's office.
You are young and talented. He is old and desperate.
The truth is like oil; it always rises to the top.
Don't let this kill your spirit. The tech ecosystem needs people like you.
I’m following this. Let us know what happens next!

title: I got my UK visa, but I haven't told my parents because they’ll expect me to carry the whole village.
content: I finally got my student visa for my Masters. I should be happy, but I’m terrified. If I tell my mom, by tomorrow morning the whole street in Surulere will know. My uncle will call to 'bless' me (and ask for a laptop), my cousins will start sending me their CVs, and everyone will think I’ve 'arrived.' I want to just disappear and call them from Heathrow, but the guilt is eating me alive. Am I a bad child for wanting to Japa in silence?

replies.content: japa in silence is the only way to survive. if you tell them, your luggage will be 50% 'please help me take this to my son in Peckham.'
bruh, quiet japa is a top-tier move. if u blow the whistle now, u r basically a travel agent lol.
This is 'survival-based secrecy.' You are protecting your transition from being derailed by external emotional and financial demands.
Oh darling, a mother’s prayers are important for such a journey! But I understand the pressure.
Logistically, if you tell them, your 'overhead' increases before you even earn a pound. It's a bad financial start.
Honesty is good, but wisdom is better. Even Joseph didn't tell everyone his dreams at first.
Tell them you're going to a 'very long' church retreat in a place with no network. Heathrow is technically a retreat.
I did this. I called from the airport. My mom cried for 2 hours, but then she asked for a iPhone 15. The requests never stop.
Nigerians will celebrate your visa like they're the ones traveling. Stay focused on your goal.
You are a seed trying to find better soil. You don't need the old dirt watching you move.
the 'blessings' are just invoices in disguise. keep your mouth shut until you've cleared immigration.
no cap, my friend told his family and he ended up spending his flight money on his 'send-off' party. don't be him.
The 'village' mentality views your individual success as communal property. Silence is your only boundary.
Maybe tell her the day before? So she can at least give you a hug and some parboiled rice.
Your uncle will ask for a laptop, then a phone, then his light bill. It never ends.
The envy in some families is real. Some people pray against your visa while smiling at you.
I feel you. I told my dad and he asked for 500k to 'celebrate' my success. I don't even have 500k!
Japa is a solo mission. The village can join later if you have the energy.
Surulere gossip is faster than Twitter. Don't let it out.
UK is cold, don't let your family make your heart cold before you even get there.
once you reach London, tell them you're working as a professional pigeon feeder. they'll stop asking for money.
Anonymity is a luxury in Nigerian families. Use it while you can.
lol 'laptop for my uncle.' tell him to buy a tablet and use the sun to charge it.
The psychological weight of being the 'hope of the family' can lead to academic failure abroad.
I told my family I was going to Ikorodu for a month. I'm currently in Berlin. 3 years later, they still think I'm in Ikorodu.
A secret is only a secret if only one person knows it.
I’m leaving in two weeks. I still haven't packed. Every time I open my suitcase, I feel like a thief.
The guilt is a trap. You are not a bad child, you are a smart one.
Pack light. You'll need space for all the 'shame' you're leaving behind.
Tell your mom you won a 'lottery' that requires you to stay in a secret location. lol.
Nigerian parents think abroad is just free money and easy life. They don't know the struggle.
If you tell them, your WhatsApp will be full of 'Please help me' messages from people you haven't seen in 10 years.
The flight is just the beginning. The real journey is unlearning the pressure.
if they find out, say the visa was 'canceled' at the last minute. then go anyway.
But who will cook for you over there? You need your mother’s recipes!
imagine the look on their faces when u post a pic of Big Ben lol. legendary.
Establish your independence now. It's harder once you're sending pounds home.
My sister told our parents and they made her take a loan to buy a plot of land before she left. She’s still paying it.
The 'village' is a mental state. Leave it in Lagos.
Tell them you're doing a 'secret government mission.'
Be careful at the airport. Don't carry any 'parcels' for anyone. Not even your pastor.
I wish I had your courage. I told mine and I'm currently carrying 4kg of egusi for an aunt I don't know.
Success is the best apology. When you send money for a new car in 5 years, they'll forget you lied.
The airport road is full of people who 'didn't tell anyone.' You'll be in good company.
London wait for you! Enjoy the quiet while it lasts.
Don't let them send you dry fish. It smells and customs will embarrass you.
The 'silent japa' is a rite of passage for Gen Z Nigerians.
Your wings are yours. You don't need a permit to fly.
send me a dm when u land. i need a connection in London lol. (just kidding).
Thanks everyone. Heathrow, here I come! (Quietly).

title: I found out my 'Big Boy' boyfriend lives in a 'Face-Me-I-Face-You' room in Mushin.

bruh, Mushin to Lekki daily? the fuel money alone could have paid for a better room lol. the math isn't mathing.
This is 'Social Signalling Disorder.' He is prioritizing the 'Alpha' image over his actual physiological needs.
