At least he’s dedicated? I can’t even be bothered to iron my shirt, and this guy is maintaining a whole alternate reality.
A life built on a lie will collapse. You are dating a character in a movie he wrote.
Did the car have a 'For Hire' sticker hidden somewhere? Many Lagos 'big boys' are just fancy Uber drivers.
Oh honey, maybe he was just ashamed? He wanted to impress a beautiful girl like you.
It’s not 'shame,' it’s fraud. People who 'package' this hard eventually expect the woman to pay for the 'upkeep.'
I dated a guy like this. Turned out the Lexus belonged to his boss who was in Dubai. The embarrassment was peak.
if he can lie about where he sleeps, he can lie about his name, his wife, and his blood type. he's a ghost.
no cap, some guys spend 90% of their income on the 'vibe' and 10% on survival. it's a Lagos lifestyle.
The crisp Agbada is the uniform of the Lagos hustler. It hides a lot of hunger.
Did you see what he ate when he got home? Probably soaked garri. The contrast is wild.
Mushin to Ikoyi is a big jump. He’s living two lives like Peter Parker.
I wonder if he pays the car wash guy to keep his secret. This is a high-maintenance lie.
Check his phone. I bet he’s in 50 'contribution' groups just to buy fuel.
You are dating a fantasy. If you confront him, he will probably blame 'the devil.'
Is his name even real? Check his ID when he’s sleeping.
Lagos is the capital of 'Fake it till you make it.' He’s just a dedicated citizen.
the car wash is his 'office.' that's where he switches from Big Boy to Mushin Boy.
The opportunity cost of his 'packaging' could have built a small business. He has poor resource management.
lol imagine him sharing a toilet then 30 mins later he's ordering 50k steak in Lekki. the range!
Insecure men often overcompensate with material displays to hide their socioeconomic anxiety.
Ask him to host you at his 'Ikoyi apartment' for a weekend. See what he says.
I want to know where he irons his Agbada. Mushin doesn't have that much light.
This is why I always check a guy's shoes. They rarely lie as well as the car.
Integrity is doing the right thing when no one is watching. He is failing.
You should have knocked on his door and asked for a cup of sugar. lol.
Mushin is a vibey place though, maybe he just likes the 'culture'? (Just kidding, he's broke).
don't ever let him 'borrow' money from you. the 'serviced apartment' is undergoing 'renovation' is the next lie.
Statistically, relationships based on false identities have a 95% failure rate within 6 months.
he's probably a 'middleman' for something. Lagos is full of them. no cap.
The 'Big Boy' trope is a patriarchal trap. It forces men into unsustainable financial behaviors.
I bet he has zero savings. All the money goes to the Lexus and the Agbada dry cleaner.
Next time he takes you to Lekki, tell him you want to eat at a bukka in Mushin. See his face.
Lies are tiring. He must be exhausted from all that acting.
How does he handle the smell of Mushin and then smell like Creed Aventus in Lekki?
The car wash is his secret base. He’s basically a broke Batman.
He's not a 'Big Boy,' he's a 'Big Actor.' Give him an Oscar and leave.
check if he's actually married in that Mushin house. that's the ultimate Lagos plot twist.
Forgive him, but don't marry him until he tells the truth. God loves a repentant heart.
if the Lexus doesn't have his name on the documents, he's a fraud. lol.
Mushin people are actually very nice. Maybe he's just ashamed of his roots.
I wonder if he uses a 'fake' accent too? 'Oh, the traffic in Ikoyi is so bad.'
The truth is better than a gold-plated lie.
Lagos dating is just an extreme sport at this point.
I broke up with him over text. He replied 'My landlord in Ikoyi is just a cousin I'm helping.' Still lying!
The 'packaging' never ends. Even at the funeral of the relationship, he's still acting.
You are free from the theater. Go find a real man.

title: My company is forcing us to wear 'Aso-Ebi' for the CEO's daughter's wedding and it costs 80k.
content: I work at a mid-sized firm in Ikeja. The HR sent a broadcast that 'all staff are expected' to buy the 80k lace for the wedding. They said it will be used for a 'group photo' with the CEO. My salary is 150k. If I don't buy it, I’ll be labeled 'not a team player' during the next appraisal. Is it legal to force employees to fund a family party?

replies.content: it's not 'Aso-Ebi,' it's an 'Appraisal Tax.' if you don't buy it, start polishing your CV because you're already fired in their hearts.
Technically, they can't deduct it from your salary without consent, but they can make your life hell. It's an informal extortion.
bruh, 80k lace? is it made of vibranium? lol. the CEO's daughter doesn't even know your name.
This is a manifestation of 'Corporate Feudalism,' where the CEO acts as a King and employees are serfs.
Just buy a 5k lace from Oshodi that looks similar. In the group photo, everyone looks the same after the 'Lagos filter' anyway.
This is why I hate 'family-run' businesses in Nigeria. The lines are too blurry.
Stand your ground. If they fire you for not buying cloth, you have a solid case for wrongful termination.
I bet the HR is getting a 'commission' from the fabric seller. That's why they are pushing it.
It's so much money, but maybe you can pay in installments? It's good to show support.
I'd rather be a 'lone wolf' than a 'team player' who is starving. 80k is too much.
80k out of 150k? that's more than 50% of your pay for a rag you'll wear once. nigerian bosses are wicked.
The 'Team Player' label is used to coerce employees into irrational financial decisions.
no cap, the CEO's daughter is probably getting a 10m wedding and u r paying for the decor lol.
What happens if you have an 'emergency' and can't come to the wedding? Try that.
80k is enough for a week's grocery in this economy. Don't do it.
I work in HR, and this is completely unethical. Report them to the labor union.
The CEO probably bought the lace for 10k and is selling it to you for 80k. Business 101.
Tell them you are allergic to that specific type of lace. Be creative.
Group photo with the CEO? Is he Jesus? Who cares!
Lagos corporate culture is just a high-budget version of village politics.
if you buy it, they'll ask for 'gift money' next. the boundary ends where you start it.
Document the HR broadcast. It's evidence of coercion.
imagine eating bread and tea for a month just to wear lace for 4 hours. lol.
This is 'forced social capital.' You are paying for a sense of belonging you haven't earned.
Rent the lace from someone else who is also forced to buy it. Share the cost!
A good boss wouldn't ask this. A great boss would buy it for the staff.
Nigerian companies and their 'family' values... it's always one-way.
If you are 'not a team player' for 80k, then let them play alone.
I hope the jollof rice at that wedding is worth 80k. (Spoiler: it won't be).
Don't let them weave your salary into their daughter's dress.
tell them you're a Jehovah's Witness and you don't do 'parties.' checkmate.
The risk of 'blacklisting' is lower than the risk of 'poverty.' Choose wisely.
80k? that's like 1000 litres of fuel. i'd rather drive than wear lace lol.
Social pressure in Nigerian workplaces is a significant cause of financial stress.
The CEO probably doesn't even know HR is doing this. Or he does and he's just greedy.
Tell them you're saving for your own wedding. They can't argue with 'culture.'
I'm a freelancer and this is why I love working from home. No Aso-Ebi, no stress.
Is there a 'white' version? Maybe you can wear an old one and hope for the best.
They are literally taxing your existence at the firm.
I'd quit. If they can't respect your 150k salary, they don't respect you.
if you go, take 5 extra boxes of food. recover your 80k by force.
Pray for a new job where they value your work, not your outfit.
imagine the CEO daughter seeing 50 employees in the same lace. she'll think it's a cult lol.
This is a classic case of 'expenditure beyond means' induced by corporate culture.
Wear the lace to every single day of work after the wedding. Make it your uniform.
A leader leads by example. If the CEO isn't paying for it, he's not a leader.
Check your employment letter. Does it say 'Aso-Ebi is mandatory'? No? Then ignore it.
Lagos life will humble you. 80k for cloth... shege.
I hope you find the courage to say no.
I’ve decided. I’m not buying it. If they fire me, I’ll see them in court. Thanks for the push.

title: I’m 'Gen Z' in a traditional office and my boss thinks my 'anxiety' is just 'disrespect.'
content: I asked for a mental health day because I was feeling overwhelmed. My boss (a typical 55-year-old 'Old School' man) laughed and said 'When we were your age, we didn't have anxiety, we just had work.' He told me I should go to church and 'pray it away' or stop 'following western trends.' I’m literally having panic attacks in the bathroom and he thinks I’m just being lazy. How do you explain boundaries to a man who thinks working 14 hours a day is a personality trait?

replies.content: bruh, the 'prayer' solution for a panic attack is so Nigerian lol. just breathe and look for a remote job.
don't explain. he won't get it. his brain is hardwired for 1985. just do your 9-5 and leave. if he talks, nod and keep scrolling.
This is a 'generational empathy gap.' He views emotional vulnerability as a threat to the rigid work-ethic hierarchy he survived.
I am so sorry. Your pain is real. Panic attacks are not a 'trend.'
You cannot change him, you can only change your environment. Peace is expensive.
Next time, just tell him you have 'running stomach.' Nigerians respect diarrhea way more than anxiety.
Oh sugar, please don't be sad. Maybe he's just stressed too? Try to bring him some meat pie.
Meat pie won't fix a toxic boss, User_02. He needs a HR complaint and a wake-up call.
The 'hustle' culture in Lagos is a slow poison. Take care of yourself first.
The machine doesn't care if the gears are crying, it only cares if they are turning. Be a human, not a gear.
no cap, the older generation thinks suffering is a badge of honor. they r traumatized and want us to be too.
asking a Nigerian boob boss for a 'mental health day' is like asking a lion for a salad. it's not going to happen.
His 'anxiety' was likely buried in 20 years of heavy drinking and emotional suppression. He’s jealous of your awareness.
Tell him your 'spirit' told you to take a day off. Use his own language against him.
Operational efficiency drops by 40% when an employee is in mental distress. He's actually hurting his own bottom line.
Lagos will break you if you don't build a shell. But your shell shouldn't be your office desk.
Mental health is not 'western.' It's biological. Your brain is an organ, just like your liver.
If you faint in that office, he'll just hire your replacement while you're in the ambulance. Leave.
Explain it like this: 'If a computer overheats, it shuts down. I am currently at 100 degrees.'
Church is good, but therapy is also good. You can do both.
if he calls you 'lazy' again, ask him why he needs 14 hours to do 8 hours of work. is he slow?
bruh, i had a panic attack at a meeting once. my boss asked if i ate bad egg roll lol.
The 'Old School' mentality conflates exhaustion with productivity. It's a fundamental error.
Print out a medical report and leave it on his desk. Nigerians respect 'official paper' more than words.
Sending you so much light. You are not alone in this Lagos madness.
Self-preservation is the first law of nature. Don't let him break it.
Is there an HR? If not, start looking for a new job immediately.
Mental health days should be in the employee handbook. Check yours.
He's probably afraid that if he acknowledges your anxiety, he'll have to acknowledge his own.
Lagos 'Senior Men' are just toddlers with grey hair and power. Don't let them win.
the moment you get a remote job, send him a 'mental health' gif and block him.
Maybe he just needs a hug? (Okay, probably not).
Productivity is a marathon, not a sprint. He's treating you like a 100m runner in a 40km race.
lol 'western trends.' like electricity and the internet? some bosses are wild.
A toxic workplace is a carcinogen for the soul.
He probably thinks therapy is just 'talking to yourself for money.'
Start a side-hustle. The more independent you are, the less his insults hurt.
Tell him your 'village people' are following you and you need a day to go and settle them. he'll agree.
God gave us doctors and healers. That includes mental health professionals.
I literally have my therapist's number as 'Electrician' in my phone so my parents won't ask questions.
if you die for this company, they will only pay for a cheap casket and your replacement starts on Monday.
The economic cost of mental health issues in Nigeria is in the billions. He's part of the problem.
bruh, just fake a high fever. it's the only language boomer bosses speak. no cap.
You are brave for even asking. Most people just suffer until they snap.
His generation survived civil wars and coups. They think if you're not bleeding, you're fine.
Lagos is a meat grinder. Don't be the meat.
I pray you find a workplace that sees your humanity.
He's not a boss, he's a taskmaster. There's a difference.
The bird that flies too long without landing will eventually fall. Land for a bit.
I just quit. I have no plan, but I have my peace. Thanks everyone.

title: My 'Landlord' just increased the rent by 50% because he saw me carrying a shopping bag from Shoprite.
content: This man is a menace. I’ve lived here for 2 years. I came home yesterday with two bags of groceries and he was sitting by the gate. This morning, I got a notice that the rent is going from 1.2m to 1.8m. His reason? 'Life is becoming sweet for you, so the house is also becoming sweet.' There was no renovation, the roof is still leaking. He literally just wants a piece of my 'perceived' wealth. Lagos landlords will show you shege.

replies.content: this is the most Lagos thing I’ve ever heard. from now on, put your Shoprite stuff in a black nylon bag from the local market. camouflage is key.
Legally, rent increases must be 'reasonable' and follow the tenancy law of the state. 50% without notice is a violation. Fight it.
bruh, 'the house is becoming sweet'? did he add sugar to the walls? lol.
Tell him you were just 'holding the bags for a friend.' Or that you found them in the trash.
This is 'proximity-based extortion.' He is monitoring your consumption to calibrate his greed.
I know a guy who parks his car two streets away so his landlord thinks he’s still trekking. The struggle is real.
It is greed, plain and simple. Do not reward it. Start looking for another place.
My landlord tried this when I bought a TV. I told him the TV was a 'gift' because I'm too broke to buy one. He backed off.
Maybe talk to him with a bottle of wine? Soften his heart a little bit?
The walls have eyes in Lagos, and they are always counting your money.
next time, walk past him while crying on the phone about 'debts.' make him feel like he should even give you a discount.
Check your contract for the 'Rent Review' clause. If it's not there, he's just gambling with your money.
next time u go shoprite, buy him a small tin of sardine and say 'this is my contribution to your retirement.' lol.
Lagos landlords are the final boss of capitalism. They don't need a reason, just a target.
Did he see the receipts? Maybe he thinks you're buying caviar instead of noodles.
I lived in a place where the landlord increased rent because I started wearing 'branded' sneakers. It's insane.
The 'perceived wealth' tax is real in Nigeria. Stay 'low-key' or stay poor.
Invite him into the room when it's raining. Let him see the 'sweetness' of the leaking roof.
He's just an old man who is jealous of your progress. Don't let him eat your fruit.
Tenancy laws in Lagos are just suggestions to these people. You need a lawyer.
if you pay that 1.8m, next year he'll see you with a pizza box and increase it to 2.5m. move now.
Market value is the only valid metric for rent increase, not your grocery list.
bruh, imagine him sitting at the gate with a calculator lol. Lagos is a movie.
This behavior creates a 'poverty trap' where individuals are discouraged from displaying upward mobility.
I'm looking for a new place. Mushin or Iyana Ipaja? Anywhere but here.
Tell him you're a 'personal shopper' and the groceries are for your rich boss.
My landlord saw my new generator and told me 'Ah, you are now a Big Man.' Next day, bill arrived.
Wickedness is a choice. He chose it.
Is the increase for the whole year? Or is he going to check your bags every month?
Don't pay. Go to the Lagos State Real Estate Regulatory Authority. They actually help.
put your Shoprite bags inside a dirty sack of rice. security by obscurity.
A 50% increase is considered 'unconscionable' in any court of law.
next time u bring food, give him one small sachet of water and say 'the economy is hard.' lol.
Information asymmetry: He thinks you have more money than you do. Correct his data.
Landlords in Nigeria act like they are shareholders in your life.
I’m a landlord and I would never do this. This man is a disgrace to the title.
Maybe he wants the house for his family and is trying to push you out?
The Shoprite bag is the 'red flag' of the middle class in Lagos. lol.
The roof leak is your leverage. Tell him no repairs, no increase.
He’s basically taxing your jollof rice. Disgusting.
bring a 'poor' looking friend to live with you for a week. let the landlord see him begging you for 100 naira.
Document the leaking roof. Take photos. Use them in your negotiations.
lol 'house becoming sweet.' is he going to lick the floor? some people are funny.
This is 'economic voyeurism.'
Tell him you got the groceries on credit and the 'Shoprite debt' is already killing you.
Stay strong. Don't let him bully you.
Imagine if you bought a car... he would probably ask for a kidney.
He's just a bully with a key. Stand up to him.
Lagos landlords need their own special place in hell.
Your 'sweet' life is your own. Don't let him taste it for free.

title: I found out my fiancée is a 'Professional Bridesmaid' and she didn't tell me.
content: We’ve been dating for 2 years. I always wondered why she was at a wedding almost every Saturday in different Aso-Ebi. I thought she just had many friends. Yesterday, I saw a website for a 'Hype-Bride Agency' and her face is the cover. She gets paid 150k per wedding to cry during the ceremony, dance behind the bride, and make the wedding look 'lively.' She says it’s just business, but I feel like I’m marrying an actress who fakes emotions for a living. Can I trust her?

replies.content: bruh, 150k to just dance and cry? where do I sign up? is there a 'Professional Groomsman' wing? lol.
she's a hustler. in this economy, you should be happy she's bringing home 600k a month from just party. don't be a killjoy.
This is 'commercialized emotional labor.' She is separating her professional performance from her personal reality. It's a skill.
Did she use your money to buy the Aso-Ebi? If the agency provides the clothes and pays her, she’s actually very financially stable.
Ask her to 'hype' your own wedding for free. Save some money on the MC! lol.
Honesty is the bedrock of marriage. If she hid a whole career from you, what else is she 'hyping'?
Lagos weddings are a performance anyway. She’s just a professional in a world of amateurs.
Oh dear, crying for strangers? That’s a bit strange. But maybe she has a soft heart.
I respect the grind. Better than her asking you for 'urgent 2k' every Friday.
A mask worn for gold is still a mask. Make sure you know the face underneath.
if she cries at your wedding, will you know if it's real or if she's just 'on the clock'?
no cap, she's probably the reason those boring weddings on IG look fun. she's a hero.
I knew a guy who did this for funerals. 'Professional Mourner.' He made bank.
The fact that she's the 'cover girl' means she's the best at it. You're marrying a star.
If she can fake a cry, she can fake a lot of things. Be careful, bro.
Does she bring home the leftover small chops? If yes, keep her.
This is actually a very common business in Asia. Interesting to see it in Lagos.
150k per Saturday? Bro, that's more than most bank managers. She's a 'Senior Woman.'
The lie is the problem, not the job. Why hide it?
She probably hid it because she knew you'd judge her. And look, you're judging her.
imagine being a 'Hype Bridesmaid' and then your own wedding is dull. the irony.
As long as she doesn't hype other men, you're fine.
next time u see her in Aso-Ebi, just say 'Work hard, baby!' lol.
The boundary between 'self' and 'service' is blurred here. It requires psychological maturity.
I hope she doesn't charge you for 'emotional support' at home.
Sit her down. Tell her you support her hustle but hate the secrecy.
Lagos girls are built different. The hustle is in the DNA.
Can she get me a job? I can dance 'Gbe Body e' very well.
The agency is probably making 500k and giving her 150k. She should start her own.
You are marrying a woman with a high EQ. She knows how to read a room.
just pray she doesn't 'hype' the divorce if things go south. lol.
God loves a cheerful giver! And she’s giving 'vibes' to the world.
Tax-wise, is she a contractor or an employee? Just kidding, this is Nigeria.
if she has 200 weddings under her belt, she's seen all the mistakes. your wedding will be perfect.
Performative joy is a staple of the Lagos social hierarchy.
I’m more interested in the 'Agency.' Do they have a branch in Abuja?
Bro, relax. It's just acting. Many people have office personas too.
Does she wear the same wig for every wedding?
I’d be more worried about all the 'best men' she meets at these weddings.
Truth is the only thing that doesn't need hype. Ask for it.
ask her to cry right now. if she does it, run. if she laughs, she's real.
The gig economy is expanding. This is just a niche service.
Imagine the 'Aso-Ebi' collection in her wardrobe. She can open a textile shop.
It’s a fascinating look into the 'economy of appearances' in Nigeria.
She’s a breadwinner. Don't fumble this.
A woman who works that hard on Saturdays is a woman of vision.
Lagos is just one big stage. We are all actors.
I bet she has a 'wedding voice' and a 'real voice.'
Tell her you found the website and see if she 'hypes' her way out of it.
We talked. She cried. I don't know if it was real, but I'm staying. The money IS good.

title: I’m addicted to 'SportyBet' and I just used my daughter's school fees to bet on a 'sure' 2-odd.
content: I’m shaking as I type this. The game was Real Madrid vs a small team. I was so sure. I put 450k (the whole school fees) into it. Madrid drew. Now the money is gone. School resumes on Monday. My wife thinks the money is in the safe. I’ve already blocked the SportyBet app, but I’m thinking of taking a loan to 'win it back.' I need help before I end it all.

replies.content: STOP. DO NOT TAKE A LOAN. 'Winning it back' is the devil's lie. You are in a hole, stop digging.
Financial desperation leads to cognitive bias. You are not thinking rationally. Call a gambling helpline now.
bruh, 450k on a draw? Madrid will always show you shege when you need them most. don't kill yourself.
Confess to your wife. The shame of confession is better than the tragedy of a loan shark.
You are experiencing 'loss aversion' and 'gambler's fallacy.' Your brain is trying to fix a mistake with a bigger mistake.
Oh my God! Please, don't do anything rash. God will provide a way, but you must stop betting!
Sell something. Your phone, your TV, your spare tire. Get that school fees back without a loan.
Loan apps in Nigeria will ruin your life. They will call your mother and your boss. Do not use them.
I lost 1m last year. I’m still paying for it. Gambling is a plague in Lagos.
The fire you used to warm yourself has burnt the house down. Don't throw more wood into it.
if you take that loan, you will bet it again. I promise you. give your phone to someone you trust.
450k... that's like 2 years of hard work for some people. shege pro max.
Go to your daughter's school. Explain you have a 'delay' and ask for a payment plan. They are human.
Madrid vs a small team? That's always a trap. Bookies love those games.
Please talk to a brother or a close friend. Don't carry this alone.
SportyBet is making billions off our tears. Stop feeding the monster.
Your daughter's education is not a 'stake.' It's her future. How could you?
The adrenaline of the bet is a drug. You are an addict. Seek therapy.
The 'sure 2-odd' is the biggest scam in history. Nothing is sure.
I’m praying for you. Please don't take your life. Money can be replaced, you cannot.
if you borrow money now, the interest will finish you. Lagos loan apps have no mercy.
The dopamine loop is broken. You need a total digital detox.
lol imagine Madrid players eating steak while u r thinking of ending it. they don't care about your slip.
The 'sunk cost fallacy' is what keeps you betting. Realize the money is gone.
Tell your wife the truth. It will be hard, but she is your partner.
Did you follow a 'tipster' on Twitter? Those guys are paid by the bookies.
Delete the app. Block the website on your router. Burn the bridges.
A man who cannot control his impulses will lose everything he loves.
I feel your pain. I lost my rent to virtual dog racing. Never again.
Lagos is full of 'Red Shops.' They are shrines of broken dreams.
if you have 5k left, buy food. do not 'try one last time.'
Financial literacy should be taught in schools. This is a tragedy.
no cap, some of us are just one 'sure bet' away from the village. stay safe.
Is your daughter in a private school? Maybe move her to a cheaper one and use the difference to pay back.
Ask your boss for a salary advance. Tell him it's a 'medical emergency.' It technically is (mental health).
You are not a bad person, you just made a very bad choice. Forgive yourself.
I hope your wife is the forgiving type. You've betrayed her trust deeply.
I’m looking at the ceiling. I can’t breathe. My wife is calling me for dinner.
Go and eat. Then tell her. Don't sleep with this lie.
The storm is loud, but the boat hasn't sunk yet. Grab the oars.
don't ever follow 'sure odds' again. if they were sure, the bookies would be broke.
Neuroplasticity means you can retrain your brain to hate gambling. Start today.
i'm praying for that draw to turn into a lesson that saves your life.
Gambling is a tax on those who are bad at math and desperate for hope.
Check your 'bet history.' See how much you've really lost. It's eye-opening.
The house always wins. Always.
Repentance starts with a change of direction. Turn around.
If you need a listening ear, we are here. Don't do anything stupid.
Lagos will still be here tomorrow. You need to be here too.
One day at a time. Just get through tonight.

title: I’m a 'Ghost Worker' for a local government and I feel guilty for taking the salary.
content: My uncle got me a job at the LG office 3 years ago. I’ve only been there twice—the day I signed and the day I did my biometrics. Every month, 85k hits my account. I actually have a real job as a graphic designer in Lekki. I see people struggling to find work, and here I am eating 'free' money from the taxpayers. I want to resign, but my uncle says I’ll 'shame' him if I do. Is this just how Nigeria works?

replies.content: bruh, 85k for doing nothing? that's just a 'national dividend' lol. enjoy it.
You are part of the 'structural leakage' that keeps this country underdeveloped. Your guilt is your conscience waking up.
This is 'institutionalized corruption.' You are a willing participant in a system that disenfranchises qualified candidates.
If you don't work, don't eat. That money is cursed because it was stolen from the public purse.
Use the 85k to help poor people. Then it's like you're a middle-man for the government's charity. lol.
Oh my, if they catch you, it will be a big problem! But many people are doing it.
If you resign, someone else will just take your spot. The seat never stays empty in an LG office.
I was a ghost worker too. I used the money to pay for my Masters. I don't regret it.
Lagos is too expensive to be having a 'moral compass' for 85k. Abeg, keep the money.
You are a shadow in a hall of light. Shadows don't build houses.
the 'shame' your uncle is talking about is that he's probably taking a cut of that 85k.
no cap, if u resign, they might even start investigating how u got the job. just stay low.
The 'Uncle' factor is why meritocracy is dead in Nigeria. It's all about 'Who you know.'
Donate the money to a motherless babies home. That way, you're not 'eating' it.
Ghost workers are why our roads have potholes. The money for bitumen is in your pocket.
I’m a civil servant and I hate people like you. We do all the work while you just get alerts.
The system is broken, but you don't have to be broken with it. Resign.
Lagos LG offices are ghost towns. You're probably not the only one.
Is there a way to actually start showing up and doing the work? Try that.
Karma is a real thing. One day, this will come back to haunt you.
85k is barely fuel money for a Lekki boy. Why are you even stressing?
If everyone had your mindset, the country would collapse. Oh wait, it already is.
lol 'shame your uncle.' nigerian elders and their 'honor' built on lies.
You are suffering from 'moral injury.' Your actions are in conflict with your values.
Does the LG have Wi-Fi? Maybe you can do your design work there and pretend to be busy.
A thief is a thief, whether he steals with a gun or a biometric thumbprint.
Nigeria is just a big 'man-know-man' arrangement. Don't kill yourself.
If you leave, your uncle will just put his girlfriend there. Nothing changes.
The change starts with us. If you want a better Nigeria, stop being part of the problem.
I bet your uncle is a big man in the party. This is how they reward their people.
put the 85k in a separate account and don't touch it. see it as a 'legal fund' for when they catch you.
Audits are becoming more frequent. 'Oronsaye Report' is coming for you.
imagine if u get promoted for doing nothing. that would be the peak of the joke lol.
The 'Ghost Worker' phenomenon is a drain on the national human capital.
My dad was a teacher and he wasn't paid for 6 months because of 'ghost workers.' Think about that.
Bro, it's 85k. That's not even enough for one night at a club in VI. Relax.
Use the money to train a young designer. Pay it forward.
The day of reckoning is coming. Don't be found on the wrong side.
The LG chairman probably has 50 ghost workers. You're just a small fish.
Your hands are dirty, even if the money is clean. Wash them.
85k... I spend that on data in a month. Abeg, keep the change.
Pray about it. If you feel peace, stay. If not, go.
lol what if they ask u to defend your 'work' one day? 'I am a ghost, I am invisible.'
Corruption is a slow-motion suicide for a nation.
If you resign, your uncle might stop talking to you. Is 85k worth your family relationship?
Integrity is what you do when no one is looking. And God is looking.
Lagos is too fast for this kind of guilt. Keep the alert hitting.
You are lucky. Most people work 14 hours for 50k.
This thread is why Nigeria won't move forward. Too many people justifying wrong.
I'm keeping it for now. I'll just use it to pay for my sister's school fees. Thanks for the debate.

title: I found out my 'spiritual' girlfriend is using a 'love charm' (Juju) on me.
content: She is very beautiful and always praying. I thought I found a 'Virtuous Woman.' But this morning, while she was in the shower, I found a small tied calabash under the bed with my name written on a piece of paper inside it, soaked in some red liquid. Ever since I met her, I’ve been obsessed—I’ve given her half my salary and stopped talking to my family. Now I’m scared to break up because I don't know what will happen to me. Am I under a spell?

replies.content: run for your life. if you found the calabash, the 'spell' is already losing power. go to a strong church and do deliverance immediately.
The spirit of deception is real. A woman who uses charms is not of God. Get out now.
bruh, 'red liquid' and your name? shege pro max. don't even pack your bags, just run lol.
This is 'coercive control' masked by folk magic. Whether the Juju is 'real' or not, the intent to manipulate you is 100% real.
Oh my Jesus! Blood of Calvary! My son, please, go and see a pastor. This is very dangerous.
Throw the calabash into the Lagoon. If she asks, say the 'Holy Ghost' took it. lol.
If you stop talking to your family, that's a huge red flag. Charms or no charms, she's isolating you.
I’ve seen this happen in my village. The man became a zombie for 10 years. Don't let it be you.
Lagos girls are not playing! From Prada to Juju real quick.
A heart that is tied by a string will eventually stop beating. Cut the string.
don't let her see you found it. pretend everything is normal, then disappear when she goes to market.
Biologically, 'obsession' can be a chemical imbalance or psychological conditioning. But the calabash is a clear indicator of intent.
no cap, some of these girls buy 'favor oil' and 'commanding tone' online. the market is huge.
Is she from a particular state? (I won't mention names but we know). lol.
Please, call your family. Tell them you are sorry and you need help.
I feel like I’m losing my mind. I still love her but I’m terrified of her.
Love shouldn't come with a calabash. That's a hostage situation.
The 'red liquid' is probably palm oil or hibiscus water, but the psychology of it is meant to break you.
If you break up, she might threaten you with more Juju. Don't believe her power.
Go to MFM. Those ones know how to handle 'tied' destinies.
if she's 'always praying,' she's probably praying to the calabash, not God.
